name: Level_2 - Task_6
description:
Estimate the finite-temperature vibrational density of states (VDOS) of bulk aluminum near 300 K from molecular dynamics. Build a periodic primitive FCC aluminum cell with conventional lattice parameter 4.05 Å and repeat it 4 × 4 × 4 to obtain 64 atoms. Use the supplied MACE-MP-0 model as an ASE calculator and keep the cell fixed throughout. Initialize Maxwell–Boltzmann velocities at 300 K, record the random seed, and remove center-of-mass momentum once before the first MD step.

Equilibrate at a target temperature of 300 K, then continue in the microcanonical (NVE) ensemble from the same cell, positions, and momenta. Do not reinitialize velocities or apply additional velocity rescaling outside the chosen equilibration thermostat. Choose suitable integrators, timesteps, thermostat settings, stage lengths, and sampling intervals. Justify equilibration using thermal traces, report the measured production temperature, and assess total-energy conservation and any drift during NVE. Preserve stage-boundary states so continuity can be checked.

Choose a defensible velocity-based spectral estimator and document any mean removal, windowing, smoothing, or mass weighting. Report frequencies in THz, the sampling interval, usable frequency range, frequency resolution, and the VDOS normalization and units. Provide a finite, nonnegative spectrum. Explain the implications of finite sampling and any unresolved limitations.

Submit a manifest linking the spectrum, thermal and energy traces, stage-boundary restart states, scripts, settings, and structured JSON analysis data. Save sampled NVE positions and velocities or momenta with atom identities, masses, times, cell information, and potential energies, together with enough metadata to reproduce the spectrum and energy checks without rerunning MD. Record the model identity and settings used.
submission_format:
Fill in the blank manifest below and submit its path inside the task workspace (for example, output/manifest.json). Linked paths may be relative to the manifest.
Fixed units and method names describe the illustrated format. Where the task leaves a method open, choose and record your method. Retain raw evidence and calculations for any alternative method; unsupported calculations require independent review before a final score.
